title: Bryan Johnson's anti-aging skincare routine: measure, protect, and keep only what moves the data
summary: Bryan tours his Blueprint skin protocol: a minimal morning routine, strict sun avoidance, and a clinic of devices (multispectral imaging, tixel, IPL/BBL, red light). His core rule is that every cream or device must prove itself on measurable markers or it is cut. Creams rarely move the data, while devices do.

principles.text: Every skincare product or device must prove itself on measurable markers or it gets cut from the protocol.
principles.quote: if we don't hit the markers the technology is out

principles.text: Creams don't move the needle on measured skin data; devices like lasers and IPL do.
principles.quote: creams don't move the needle on data

principles.text: Avoid sun damage: stay out of high-UV hours, use sunscreen when outside, and cut UV at home with window tint.
principles.quote: the most effective thing to do is avoid the damage if you're going to be outside wear sunscreen

principles.text: Use clinical-grade multispectral imaging to track UV damage, pores, reds and browns instead of judging by eye.
principles.quote: UV damage which you can't see with your eye it's on a machine using multi-spectral Imaging

principles.text: Keep the daily routine simple: wash, apply a trial cream, then sunscreen.
principles.quote: in summary the routine is very simple I wash with this in the morning I put this cream on

principles.text: Keep red light therapy (3x/week, 12 minutes) on evidence of general benefit even when its effect can't be measured directly.
principles.quote: I do this uh three times a week uh for 12 minutes so it's a total of uh 36 minutes a week
